question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: prior-ratio retrieval, ratio identification, useful-output calculation, reverse input solving, reverse energy accounting, changed-input comparison, then a fair comparison of two operating systems

evidence_basis.originality_note: Every context, value, wording and data combination is original. The set adapts only the controlled assessment demands of identifying useful output and input, direct and reverse ratios, same-interval energy and power, and multi-stage efficiency.

questions.prompt: State the relationship used to calculate the efficiency of an energy-conversion system. State the possible range of efficiency as a percentage.
A loudspeaker receives 240 J of electrical energy and transfers 36 J usefully as sound. Which expression gives its efficiency?
A steriliser receives 2.5 kJ of energy and is 68% efficient. What is its useful energy output?
A motor is 60% efficient and provides a useful output power of 480 W. What is its total input power?
An automatic door transfers 1.62 kJ usefully during one opening cycle. Its efficiency is 67.5%.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total input energy for the opening cycle.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the energy transferred to non-useful stores during the opening cycle.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use your answers to state an energy-conservation check for the opening cycle.

questions.prompt: A hydraulic tool initially receives 75 kJ and transfers 48 kJ usefully. After a modification, it delivers the same useful output while its total input energy is reduced by 12%.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the initial percentage efficiency of the tool.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the initial energy transferred to non-useful stores.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the modified total input energy and hence the modified percentage efficiency.

questions.prompt: Two workshop machines operate steadily. Machine A has a total input power of 2.5 kW and an efficiency of 72%. Machine B delivers 2.0 kW of useful power while transferring 0.80 kW in non-useful ways.

figure.purpose: Assess a fair comparison when useful output size and efficiency may suggest different rankings.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white learner comparison diagram with two separate machine boxes. Label Machine A input 2.5 kW and efficiency 72 percent. Label Machine B useful output 2.0 kW and non-useful output 0.80 kW. Leave the missing powers and comparison conclusion blank. Show no formulas or answers.
figure.alt_text: Machine A has 2.5 kilowatts input and 72 percent efficiency, while Machine B has 2.0 kilowatts useful output and 0.80 kilowatts non-useful output.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the useful output power of Machine A.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total input power of Machine B.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the percentage efficiency of Machine B.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: State which machine is more efficient and explain why Machine B's larger useful output power does not determine the answer by itself.
